nodes.description: Address with admin privileges; authorizes queue, cancel and execute operations and can be replaced via the pendingAdmin handshake.
Address nominated to become the next admin through acceptAdmin.
Secondary role allowed to queue transactions but not to execute or cancel them.
Minimum delay in seconds that must elapse between queueing and executing a transaction.
One-time bootstrap flag allowing the deployer admin to set pendingAdmin directly.
Mapping of transaction hashes to their queued flag, used to gate execution.
Constant 14 day window after eta during which a queued transaction may still be executed.
Constant 24 hour lower bound for the timelock delay.
Constant 30 day upper bound for the timelock delay.
Sets initial admin, operator, delay and admin_initialized while enforcing MINIMUM_DELAY and MAXIMUM_DELAY.
Empty receive function that lets the contract accept ETH.
Self-call only function updating the timelock delay within the allowed range.
Self-call only function replacing the operator role.
Lets pendingAdmin become admin and clears pendingAdmin.
Sets pendingAdmin; self-call gated once admin_initialized is true, otherwise requires admin and flips the flag.
Admin or operator queues a transaction hash with an eta beyond current time plus delay.
Admin cancels a previously queued transaction hash.
Admin executes a queued, matured and not stale transaction, forwarding value to an arbitrary target via a low-level call.
Internal view helper returning block.timestamp, used for all timelock comparisons.
Caller controlled address used in every authorization check.
Miner influenced block timestamp driving timelock maturity and staleness checks.
target.call{value:value}(callData) forwards arbitrary native value and calldata to an attacker supplied address, enabling reentrancy and arbitrary execution.
Timelock maturity and GRACE_PERIOD gating performed purely on block.timestamp, enabling timestamp dependence.
